lines.text: Fire is extremely dangerous and we must all be
cautious of it to save our lives and the lives of our loved
ones. Depending on the existing condition, fire may
start as a slow-growth scenario or it may grow rapidly
in a building. In either instance, fire is considered as
a disaster which when not suppressed can lead to a
total loss of properties and ultimately the loss of lives.
Nowadays and in the future generations, it is
important to have a basic understanding on fire
safety and prevention. Bureau of Fire Protection is the
sole agency mandated to enforce the Fire Code of
the Philippines. As such, public safety is its highest
obligation and prevention of destructive fires is among
The Bureau of Fire Protection always emphasizes the immense
importance of our commitment to ensure the safety of our
people against destructive fires. I commend the dedication
of every man and woman of the BFP, who tirelessly give their
due diligence and hard work in the conduct of fire safety
inspections and building plan evaluation. This guidebook is a
product of our agency’s desire to standardize our processes

Fire safety inspection and building plan evaluation are some of the
most crucial undertakings in BFP’s fire code enforcement and fire
safety capacities. BFP, being an agency primarily responsible for
securing a fire safe nation, sees the importance of firmly enforcing
the RA 9514 otherwise known as the Fire Code of the Philippines of
2008 and its Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations (RIRR).
It is with great pride and privilege as Director for Fire Safety and
Enforcement that it is during my time another remarkable
accomplishment in fire safety materialized, the “Fire Safety
Guidelines on Different Type of Occupancy Volume 2”, an
additional reference guide that will greatly aid our BFP Fire Safety
Enforcers especially our fire safety inspectors and building plan
evaluators in assessing and identifying hazards and ease the
challenge in the issuance of recommendations during the
preparation of After Inspection Report and Building Plan Evaluation
The Fire Safety Enforcement Division under the leadership of Engr.
Ariel T. Miranda, the people behind this initiative, has shown
carried into these pages. It is a pleasure to work with a team
who knows the value of securing a fire safe environment.
There is no single prescription for improving fire safety inspection, but
this handbook provides principles and tested practices to bring its
vision to life, off of these pages and into reality. May this reference guide
truly serve its purpose and that the knowledge we will acquire from
this publication would be properly applied into practice imperatively.
Through this primer, BFP are also given yet another opportunity to
become true advocates of fire safety and to demonstrate the spirit
of our organizational motto, “To Save Lives and Properties”. It is our
hope that we in the DFSE would continue to have the privilege of
partnering with the community in promoting fire safety through
scrupulous fire code and other law enforcement to ensure a fire safe
Director for Fire Safety and Enforcement
Implementing Rules and Regulations (RIRR) of Republic Act 9514
took effect. Since then, the Office of the Fire Safety Enforcement
Division (FSED) under my supervision, exerted great efforts to
cascade the salient features of the RIRR throughout all regions
Truly, it was never an easy task to inform and educate our field
personnel about the enforcement of the Fire Code. Nonetheless, it is
a great privilege to have been given the chance and opportunity to
impart ample knowledge and principles about the Fire Code to our
comrades in the Bureau of Fire Protection.
This guidebook entitled “Fire Safety Guidelines on the Different Type
of Occupancies Volume II” is another accomplishment of the FSED
under the abled leadership of CSUPT MANUEL G GOLINO, Director
for Fire Safety and Enforcement. Indeed it is a fact that the Fire Code
and its RIRR is a complex topic to comprehend. With the help of
this guidebook, we hope that fire safety enforcers will have a holistic
understanding on the standards in fire safety and prevention. This
guidebook summarizes all the fire safety standards of different types
of occupancies in line with the RIRR. Having such, our personnel in
the field can easily implement the provisions of the Fire Code and its
In these modern times, let us never take fire easy because it can
destroy everything. Let us all be proactive and cautious with fire. As
they always say, prevention is better than cure. Similarly, we must
highlight and practice fire prevention in our day to day lives to avoid
As the Chief of the Fire Safety Enforcement Division, it is again my pride
and honor to offer everyone the second volume of this guidebook.
May this piece be a helping hand in attaining the mission of the Bureau
of Fire Protection to enforce the Fire Code and to attain its vision to
become a modern fire service fully capable of ensuring a fire-safe nation.
ENGR. ARIEL T. MIRANDA, REE, DFSE, PGCOSH
